o1.biggest_strength: A dated first-30-days plan the one partner manager can run, with owners. It sits alongside lifetime maths, a clear no to the 20% cut, a one-page rules list with disclosure wording, and a perk budget for creator-educators.
o1.biggest_mistake: Some figures are unsupported or muddled: the "$38,000 saving" and the 1,250 / 3,365 customer estimates are invented, and the break-even range mixes revenue with an assumed margin. The first-30-days table also sits oddly with the 30 Nov payout pull-forward and the 1 Jan start dates. The extra Podia-specific legal detail is useful but adds length.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Drop the shaky derived numbers or show them plainly. Keep the single rate and the 90-day window, and state the cost range clearly. Tighten the word count, and make sure the first-30-days dates and the payout pull-forward line up with the January start.

o2.biggest_strength: A straight, well-reasoned no to the 20% cut. It gives the break-even at a 12.5% revenue fall, the $1,677 vs $1,130 lifetime maths, the top-20 concentration and the rival's 40% offer, then builds a 40%-for-12-months Partner tier that rewards the top creators without raising cost across the board.
o2.biggest_mistake: The first-30-days plan uses day ranges rather than dates. The 90-day window cost is only given as a sensitivity (about $63,000 per 10% rise) rather than a single estimate. The $46,000 cost for the 40% Partner tier applies the uplift to all of the top-20 revenue, which is rough.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Give calendar dates in the 30-day plan. Add one clear total for the cost of the 90-day window plus the 40% tier. Put the lower minimum and faster payouts at the very start of the plan, and say what the $40,000 does for non-top-20 affiliates.

reason: Both say no to the 20% cut and build the plan around the top 20, the 90-day window and payout fixes. Output 2 has cleaner maths, a sensible 40%-for-12-months top tier that answers the rival offer, and plain wording. Output 1 has better dates but some invented figures.
